players.product: enterprise PCIe Gen5 SSD controllers for hyperscaler SSDs

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 IR deck roadmap: PCIe 6.0 controller FC6161 (Gen6) in 2026 at 28,500 MB/s sequential read and write, 6,900 KIOPS random read and 1,000 KIOPS random write, shown as x2 the performance of the Gen5 controller (14,000 / 11,000 MB/s, 3,400 / 500 KIOPS); Q4 2025 results included KRW 11 Bil. of NRE expenses for the PCIe Gen6 controller
quarterly_data.figure: Gen6 FC6161: 28,500 MB/s; 6,900 KIOPS; Q4 2025 Gen6 NRE KRW 11 Bil.

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 (unaudited, per the deck): revenue KRW 59,538 million, up 149.4% QoQ and 209.8% YoY; operating profit KRW 7,686 million vs a KRW 29,494 million loss in Q4 2025 (turn to profitability); Q4 2025 included KRW 24 Bil. of advance payments received
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 revenue KRW 59,538 million (+149.4% QoQ, +209.8% YoY); operating profit KRW 7,686 million

quarterly_data.signal: Company strategy per the deck: controllers are qualified with NAND manufacturer partners over 1.5+ years and then supplied for a stable 3~5 years; FADU is actively pursuing the majority of leading hyperscalers as customers alongside the top 6 NAND manufacturers, diversifying across hyperscalers and server OEMs through strategic NAND partnerships; the company says incumbent controller vendors with legacy architectures are losing ground. Controllers support both TLC and QLC; the power-solution line (PLP, multi-channel PMIC) started in 2025
